issues.title: Local stability theorem presented as a guarantee for all tested starts

failure_location.quote: Numerical results on both 1D and 2D systems demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach, with comprehensive validation through multiple initial conditions showing that all closed-loop trajectories converge exponentially to the origin from various starting points, successfully stabilizing unstable equilibria with theoretical guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims theoretically guaranteed exponential convergence for all reported trajectories from the various tested starting points. The old paper actually proves only that there exists an unspecified r>0 for which the conclusion holds when ||x0||<r; it never computes r or proves that the reported one- and two-dimensional initial-condition grids lie in that neighborhood. The tables and figures provide finite-time numerical observations, not a theorem extending the guarantee to those grids. The material difference is theoretical certification versus empirical behavior consistent with a local result.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion overstate the geographic scope of the stability guarantee. The local theorem itself is not enlarged by this prose, and the empirical convergence observations remain observations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Revise every abstract, introduction, conclusion, caption, and numerical-discussion statement that links the tested initial-condition grids to Theorem thm:stability. State that the theorem guarantees exponential convergence only for starts satisfying ||x_0||<r for an unspecified local radius, while the tables and figures report finite-time numerical decay consistent with that local result; do not claim that the tested grids are certified unless an explicit basin estimate containing them is proved.
issues.why_classification: The repair is editorially local and leaves the formal local theorem and numerical observations intact, but it necessarily withdraws the substantive claim that every tested start has a theoretical certificate. That is a limited weakening from certification to empirical evidence, so it exceeds a minor same-guarantee correction without requiring global reconstruction.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: The local exponential stability conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:stability} therefore applies as stated, and the rapid trajectory decay reported in each subsection ($\|x(T)\| < 10^{-9}$ at the integration horizon) is consistent with this guarantee.

issues.title: Unsupported value-function and control suboptimality bounds

failure_location.quote: Since $V^*(x_0) \leq J(x_0; \hat{u})$, we have $V^*(x_0) \leq \hat{V}(x_0) + \epsilon \cdot T(x_0)$, giving the upper bound.

issues.failure_explanation: From the displayed differential inequality, integration gives J(x0;hat u) >= hat V(x0)-hat V(x(T))-epsilon T, not the displayed upper bound on J. Even accepting that displayed upper bound, V*(x0) <= hat V(x0)+epsilon T implies hat V(x0)-V*(x0) >= -epsilon T, not the claimed upper bound. Moreover, T is defined through the optimal trajectory whereas the calculation follows the approximate feedback trajectory. Consequently neither the two-sided value estimate nor the dependent control-cost estimate follows.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised O(epsilon T) value-function estimate and the dependent control-suboptimality corollary are unestablished under the stated one-sided residual hypothesis. The preceding LMI construction is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace thm:suboptimality and cor:control_suboptimality together by a sign-correct verification result. With R denoting the displayed HJB residual, assume the relevant trajectories remain in the domain and satisfy the needed terminal limits, and require 0<=R(x)<=epsilon*w(x), where T_hat(x_0):=integral_0^infinity w(x_hat(t))dt is finite (or include the corresponding stopping-time and terminal-tail terms). Completion of squares gives L+dVhat/dt=R+(1/2)(u-uhat)^T D(u-uhat), hence Vhat<=V*, J(x_0;uhat)=Vhat(x_0)+integral R(x_hat(t))dt, and therefore 0<=V*(x_0)-Vhat(x_0)<=epsilon*T_hat(x_0) and 0<=J(x_0;uhat)-V*(x_0)<=epsilon*T_hat(x_0). Define T_hat using the approximate closed-loop trajectory, not the optimal trajectory.
issues.why_classification: The old one-sided lower residual bound yields the opposite cost inequality, and the same error propagates to the corollary. A comparable value-error and control-suboptimality chain can be recovered by a contained standard verification argument, but only after materially strengthening the residual control, reversing the value ordering, and correcting the trajectory and terminal bookkeeping. This is nontrivial limited repair rather than global reconstruction or major loss.

issues.title: Unjustified quadratic coercivity and rate in the stability theorem

failure_location.quote: For stabilizable/detectable pairs, we have $q(x) \geq c_3 \|x\|^2$ for some $c_3 > 0$ near the origin.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Taking $\alpha = \sqrt{c_2/c_1}$ and $\beta = c_3/(2c_2)$ gives the result.

issues.failure_explanation: For example, q(x1,x2)=x1^2+x2^4 is positive away from zero, while Q=diag(2,0). With the controllable double-integrator pair A=[[0,1],[0,0]], B=(0,1)^T, the pair (A,Q^{1/2}) is observable and hence detectable, but q(0,t)/||(0,t)||^2=t^2 tends to zero, so no positive c3 exists. Separately, the proof obtains beta=c3/(2c2), asymptotically c3/lambda_max(P), and supplies no relation that would yield lambda_min(P)/lambda_max(P). A scalar stable system with decay rate below one also directly contradicts that universal eigenvalue-ratio rate.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not establish local exponential decay from the standing assumptions, and its advertised quantitative rate is unsupported. Examples with a strictly positive quadratic cost may satisfy the added condition, but that does not repair the old theorem's stated scope.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Preserve the standing model scope by replacing the coercivity argument with a closed-loop linearization proof. Explicitly take P to be the stabilizing Riccati solution; then the feedback linearization is A_cl=A-BD^{-1}B^T P, which is Hurwitz under the stabilizability/detectability hypotheses, and smoothness gives local exponential stability of the nonlinear closed loop. Delete the universal bound beta>=lambda_min(P)/lambda_max(P) and instead allow any decay exponent below the stability margin -max Re sigma(A_cl), or state a valid bound obtained from a Lyapunov equation for A_cl.
issues.why_classification: A contained standard argument recovers the theorem's central local exponential-stability conclusion without falsely deriving quadratic coercivity from detectability. However, the advertised eigenvalue-ratio rate is genuinely false and must be replaced by a different, system-dependent rate. The resulting quantitative weakening is meaningful but limited, making the issue moderate.

issues.title: Positive definiteness does not follow in the uncontrolled reduction

failure_location.quote: where $P = \nabla^2 V(0) \succ 0$ (positive definite since $A$ is stable by assumption).

issues.failure_explanation: Setting B=0 correctly yields A^T P+PA+Q=0, but under the stated assumptions its unique solution need only be positive semidefinite. An admissible scalar counterexample is f(x)=-x, g=0, and q(x)=x^4: A=-1 is Hurwitz, (A,0) is detectable, q is smooth and positive away from zero, and the HJB equality has V=x^4/4. Here Q=0 and the Lyapunov equation gives P=0, so the asserted P positive definite is false.
issues.overall_effect: Part 3 of the reduction theorem and the associated claim that the Hessian constraint necessarily excludes the trivial solution in this uncontrolled detectable regime are unsupported. The algebraic reduction from the Riccati equation to the Lyapunov equation remains valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For the full stated uncontrolled regime, replace P≻0 in Part 3 by P≽0 and use P=integral_0^infinity e^{A^Tt}Qe^{At}dt. State separately that P is positive definite precisely under observability of (A,Q^{1/2}) (with Q≻0 as a sufficient condition), not merely because A is Hurwitz and the pair is detectable. Qualify the accompanying prose to say that the Hessian equality need not exclude V identically zero when P is singular.
issues.why_classification: The Lyapunov reduction itself survives through a short correction, but positive definiteness and the claimed trivial-solution exclusion fail on a natural allowed class of higher-order costs such as q(x)=x^4. Losing that nondegeneracy guarantee is mathematically meaningful, though a recognizably comparable reduction theorem remains without new global architecture.

issues.title: Internally inconsistent 1D exact benchmark

failure_location.quote: where the state cost $q(x)$ is chosen such that a polynomial value function $V^*(x) = x^2 + 0.25x^4$ satisfies the HJB equation exactly.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the displayed q is an admissible state cost making the displayed V* the exact optimal value for the standing problem. In fact, V*'(x)=2x+x^3 and f(x)=x+x^3 give q(x)=0.5(V*')^2-V*'f=-x^4-0.5x^6, which is negative for every nonzero x and contradicts the standing positivity assumption. In addition, V*''(0)=2, whereas the experiment imposes P=1+sqrt(3). Thus the HJB identity is being applied to an inadmissible and Riccati-incompatible data tuple, not to the claimed exact optimal-control benchmark.
issues.overall_effect: The old 1D experiment cannot validate exact value-function recovery or optimal-control accuracy in the stated problem class, and its reported approximation and constraint comparisons use mutually incompatible targets. The abstract theoretical results do not depend on this benchmark.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the 1D benchmark by a self-consistent exact polynomial problem and rerun all associated optimization and simulations. For example, retain f(x)=x+x^3 and the imposed Riccati value by setting p=1+sqrt(3), V*(x)=(p/2)x^2+(1/2)x^4, and q(x)=x^2+(p-2)x^4. Then q is positive away from zero, the HJB equality holds identically, V*''(0)=p, q''(0)=2, and 2p-p^2+2=0. Recompute every value/control error, constraint check, trajectory, table, figure, and validation claim from the corrected data.
issues.why_classification: The old numerical claims cannot be repaired by relabeling a coefficient because the SDP constraint, exact target, Riccati constraint, and all reported errors are mutually inconsistent. Nevertheless, a directly checkable benchmark with the same scalar unstable polynomial dynamics and an exact quartic optimum is available through a contained data reconstruction and numerical reoptimization. That is substantial local repair, not global reconstruction.

issues.title: Internally inconsistent 2D radial benchmark
issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims an exact admissible optimum for f(x)=x(1+||x||^2) with V*(x)=||x||^2+0.25||x||^4. The HJB equality uniquely forces q(x)=0.5||grad V*||^2-grad V*·f=-||x||^4-0.5||x||^6, which is negative away from the origin and violates the standing state-cost assumption. Also, the claimed value has Hessian 2I at the origin, not the imposed Riccati matrix (1+sqrt(3))I. Hence the experiment cannot simultaneously have the advertised exact value, positive running cost, and Hessian constraint.
issues.overall_effect: The 2D experiment does not validate optimal-value approximation or Riccati matching for the stated control problem. Its empirical trajectories may still be numerical observations, but the claimed exact benchmark and associated error comparisons are invalid. The general formal framework is not dependent on this example.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the 2D experiment by a self-consistent exact radial benchmark and rerun its SDP and simulations. One contained choice retains f(x)=x(1+||x||^2) and the original Riccati matrix: with p=1+sqrt(3), set V*(x)=(p/2)||x||^2+(1/2)||x||^4 and q(x)=||x||^2+(p-2)||x||^4. Then q>0 away from zero, the HJB equality holds, the Hessian is pI, Q=2I, and 2pI-p^2I+2I=0. Replace all approximation errors, Hessian checks, trajectories, tables, figures, and optimality claims by results from this corrected run.
issues.why_classification: The claimed exact optimum and every optimal-value or Riccati comparison based on it are invalid, so a mere wording edit is insufficient. However, the same radial unstable system admits an explicit positive-cost quartic benchmark of the same mathematical type, making a contained reconstruction and reoptimization possible. A comparable 2D validation can therefore survive without global proof changes or major mathematical loss.
